title: Patriotism
text: And so the Fiancée kidnapping incident schemed up by Three Heroes Church was suppressed in an instant, I say. But it was obvious that another problem would immediately rear its head. I had certainly gotten a firm verbal promise, but it seemed the withdrawal of Father’s wanted status within the country was being delayed quite badly. The Fiancée had also given orders to her subordinates about it. Before that fact became clear, I went to see Rafumi while concealed. When I did, Rafumi was resting in a room with Ren’s companions, disguised as Ren, apparently giving them some sort of warning.
“You lot had best refrain from acting alone too much. Kuro, you need to be careful too.”
“Hmm?”
“For what reason?”

“Apparently, when a country schemes to sow discord among the heroes, one tactic is to have someone kill a companion to incite them. Given the current state of Melromarc’s shadow organizations, this is a prime opportunity for them to use that method.”
With a visible chill, the leader of Ren’s companions broke into a cold sweat. Then they exchanged glances with each other.
“W-we’ll keep that firmly in mind.”

“More than anything, Three Heroes Church is running short of manpower to pull off various misdeeds. Given their current push to conscript soldiers through hatred of demi-humans and beastmen, even I can’t rule out them doing something beyond my calculations. Though it is rather interesting, gathering data on what they’ll get up to.”
Rafumi, disguised as Ren, laughed wickedly. Kukuku…
“Ohh.”
Kuro’s eyes sparkled at the sight. Was that some sort of chuunibyou appeal?
“Right? Spear Hero.”
“Indeed,” I said.
I revealed myself in a flash and nodded.
“It would be prudent to get the Queen back here quickly, I say.”

“I judge it more advantageous in the long run to do a bit more cleaning up before she returns. If she comes back now, it’ll just be a hassle. We need to crush Three Heroes Church’s reputation, don’t we?”

That was the thought, but it was a rather precarious line to walk as to whether it would go well. Well, worst case, we could just flee the country via portal. The safety of Filo-tan and the Fiancée was the top priority, I say. With that settled, Rafumi stood by at the castle… and the incident where Three Heroes Church would reveal its true colors and cause an uproar simply had time pass by as is. As expected, the situation where the withdrawal of Father’s wanted status kept being delayed and delayed continued for a while. On top of that, what arrived from the Guild to Rafumi disguised as Ren were reports of arson and pillaging by the Shield Hero in various towns and villages across Melromarc.
“That shield devil! We won’t let him destroy our beloved Melromarc! Everyone! Let’s unite and volunteer for the nation!”
“Ohh!”

It seemed Three Heroes Church’s aim was to drag Father’s image down as far as possible, and then recruit citizens overflowing with righteous indignation and patriotism as soldiers. In town after town, it seemed the flow of citizens volunteering as soldiers was increasing because of this. What’s more, Three Heroes Church had apparently issued a statement.
“All heroes save the Sword Hero are impostors—beastmen who’ve fallen under the Shield Hero’s influence! Everyone! Protect the world from their machinations!”
“Ohh!”
“Let us bring judgment upon the demi-humans and beastmen who stole away our beloved families!”
“Ohh!”

Melromarc seemed to be steadily dyeing itself in an increasingly ominous atmosphere. If we didn’t perform good deeds, it would become difficult to stop Three Heroes Church’s propaganda campaign. That sort of information apparently flowed through to Father via Lazy Pig as well. Beloved families, they say—were they referring to the Three Heroes Church followers disguised as bandits? A fitting end for someone who’d plotted to attack a caravan out of misplaced grudge.
“Sounds like they’re ignoring the castle’s official notices. They sure are persistent with all sorts of tricks… I guess manipulating public perception really matters.”
“The demon king of all evil in this world, the Shield Devil, is it? Rough go of it, Naofumi-san. Honestly, wouldn’t destroying this country be better for the world?”
Itsuki said this with a look of contempt upon hearing that information.
“It’s just that public sentiment is being steered in a bad direction, that’s all. So, did Melty-chan and the King actually try to withdraw my wanted status like they said they would?”
“I did get a verbal promise, I say.”

“Ah, that’s what she said too? By the way, that King is currently desperately trying to protect the demi-human he was entrusted with from Three Heroes Church’s machinations within the castle. Seems he’s figured out through sheer atmosphere alone that his life’s being targeted.”

Trash had apparently taken Tiger Girl to his private chambers, keeping his eyes sharp so that any strange assassins who came would be struck down in turn. He was also extremely concerned about the Fiancée. It seemed he was barely getting any sleep.

“I only know the broad strokes, but wasn’t she a demi-human important to that King? Well, even an idiot would understand it’s dangerous to try something like that right in the heart of the country, right under the noses of the higher-ups—nice way to buy time.”
Itsuki was chuckling as well.
“So the King’s fighting a lone battle, huh… well, part of me wants to see it play out, but thinking about the girl I entrusted to him makes me uneasy.”
“I agree on that point. We can’t let anything actually happen to her.”
“By the way… Rafumi-chan, Motoyasu-kun. A kid named Fohl came storming into our base over in Zeltoble—any idea what that’s about?”
Rafumi swiftly averted her gaze under the pressure of Father’s smile. Since she’d been away, she’d only protected Tiger Girl and handed her over to Trash. And as usual, someone had come charging in.
“Apparently he’s the older brother of the girl entrusted to that King? It’d be great if you two could arrange a meeting sooner rather than later, because things are getting rough on our end?”
“Interesting, isn’t it? A siscon comrade for the King.”

“That kind of thing isn’t really all that interesting, no… Lars-chan happened to be around so she managed to restrain him, but now she’s asking me just what exactly happened? Her adoptive father seemed to have already guessed.”
Now that I thought of it, Panda had been anonymously giving part of her earnings to the tiger siblings. So Panda must have guessed it was that particular pair of siblings.
“Got it. Then let’s get them to meet up quickly. This has provided us with some rite-of-passage-style entertainment on our end too.”
“Objectively it might be interesting, but please stop it. Honestly… just when a wave’s about to occur, too…”

Things being in such a whirlwind of activity—that’s exactly what this was. But thinking about it… staying put in Melromarc without earning any fame led to exactly this sort of situation. It felt like being driven right into the trap Three Heroes Church wanted. Well, if they came strutting up spouting nonsense about holy war, I figured we could just wipe them all out and eliminate the troublemakers in one go. That moment was probably just a little ways off. In any case, Rafumi seemed to have brought Tiger Guy to the castle and let him meet Trash. I’d confirmed this part myself too, but since there’d been a similar exchange before, it didn’t leave much of an impression on me. Still, within the castle, the ministers seemed to harbor growing distrust toward Trash, and here and there I could hear whispers like “That King has been won over by the demi-humans and beastmen now” and “That shield devil… such underhanded persuasion” and “Having a Hakuko within our castle—an unprecedented scandal since the founding of Melromarc.”
It had become plain as day that Trash’s position was falling apart. And so… the time for the wave drew near.
“So how should we handle this round’s wave in Melromarc?”
The heroes gathered for a strategy meeting inside the circus over in Zeltoble.
“I’ll sink it in a flash, I say.”
Since there was no doubt this was a wave Rival might show up to, I had to sink it quickly before she could get here.
“That’s probably the safest bet.”
“I’ll bring back souvenirs, of course. Some for Fleon-chan’s meals too, I say.”
“Ah, I recall hearing something about that.”
“Hand over some of the materials.”
“I’ll spare you some, I say.”

They were materials I no longer needed anyway. Might as well share with Father and the others. Thinking that, I turned my eyes toward Itsuki. Back then… I’d sunk the wave in a flash, and at the same time Itsuki had attacked, only for me to strike him down and take him captive. That he was now here participating in our strategy meeting—that really said something about how much circumstances could change.
